mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points within a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when the FEDFUNDS rate decreases by more than 0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within three months signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when the UNRATE increases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1% in the same period, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 quarters and INDPRO decreases > 1%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 shows negative growth for two quarters and INDPRO decreases by more than 1%.
